title: Normalized strict finite-pullback Roos augmentation
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension, and let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Work with the completed coefficient module categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $g^*_{\rm mod}$ for ordinary coefficient-linear pullback with its specified adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For a cochain complex $C$ over $Y$, let $P_g(C)$ be the strict tower whose nth term is the finite pullback of the ordinary reduction of $C$ modulo exponent $n+1$, restricted to completed coefficients on $X$, with the actual quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $B_g(C)=\prod_{n\geq0}P_g(C)_n$ and $T_g(C)=\operatorname{mappingCocone}(1-s:B_g(C)\to B_g(C))$, using the recorded product, tower shift and mapping-cocone convention. For $x\in C^i(V)$ denote its module-pullback unit image by $\iota_g(x)$ and its reduction-unit image by $1\otimes x$.

There is a unique natural transformation $\alpha:(g^*_{\rm mod})^{\rm complex}\to T_g$ such that for every $C,i,n,V,x$ its product projection satisfies $(\pi_n\operatorname{fst}\alpha_C)^i(\iota_g(x))=\iota_{g,n}(1\otimes x)$, where $\iota_{g,n}$ is the finite module-pullback unit followed by completed-coefficient restriction, and its shifted mapping-cocone component is zero in every degree. If $g$ is an isomorphism, $C$ is K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $Q(C)$ belongs to the intrinsic bounded constructible derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], then $Q(\alpha_C)$ is an isomorphism. All normalization equations are strict chain-level equations.

source.place: Natural Weil isomorphism on coefficient twists; the explicit sheaf-level and derived normalization and complete proof are already recorded in lean/Sheaf/Paper/FrobeniusCoefficientTwistsCanonical.lean at WeilConjectures.FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.existsUnique_pullbackAugmentation, WeilConjectures.FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.pullbackAugmentation, WeilConjectures.FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.pullbackAugmentation_isIso. The general construction is the one in these existing declarations, with the isomorphism-derived-pullback normalization cited there.

proof.text: For each positive quotient reduce a section x to 1 tensor x and apply the finite module-pullback adjunction unit. The coefficient projection equations make these maps completed-linear, and naturality in sections and complexes gives morphisms commuting with differentials and every strict tower transition.

Their product is killed by 1 minus the tower shift. The mapping-cocone lift with zero shifted component is therefore a chain map. The same construction commutes with chain maps, giving a natural transformation. The pullback adjunction and the sheafified tensor presentation determine each finite component from the specified generators; product joint monicity and the two mapping-cocone projections prove uniqueness.

When g is an isomorphism, identify its inverse image with exact relabelling along the equivalent pro-etale site. This relabelling preserves products, the normalized coefficient quotients, and their strict transitions. Thus it identifies the specified augmentation with the derived-completeness unit of the relabelled complex. Exact countable products identify the strict Roos mapping-cocone with the derived inverse limit. The finite-free completed comparison, with coefficient extension E to itself, states invertibility of precisely this zero-shifted-component unit on a derived-complete input. Constructibility supplies derived completeness, and the good-complex hypotheses identify ordinary reductions with derived reductions. Hence Q(alpha_C) is invertible.

theorem existsUnique_pullbackAugmentation (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃! eta : (modulePull l E g).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶
        integralOperationsPullbackComplexFunctor l E g,
      (∀ (C : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E Y) ℤ)
        (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (V : Y.ProEt) (x : (C.X i).val.obj (op V)),
        (((eta.app C).f i ≫
          (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst
            (towerTransitionEndomorphism
              (K := fun j ↦ ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor
                l E g).obj C).obj (op j))
              (integralOperationsTowerStep
                ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor
                  l E g).obj C)))).f i ≫
          (Pi.π (fun j ↦ ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor
            l E g).obj C).obj (op j)) n).f i).val.app
              (op ((proEtaleBaseChange g).obj V)))
          (moduleSection l E g (C.X i) V x) =
            integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E g n
              (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y n).obj
                C).X i) V
              (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E Y n
                (C.X i) (op V) 1 x)) ∧
      ∀ (C : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E Y) ℤ)
        (i : ℤ),
        (eta.app C).f i ≫
          (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd
            (towerTransitionEndomorphism
              (K := fun j ↦ ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor
                l E g).obj C).obj (op j))
              (integralOperationsTowerStep
                ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor
                  l E g).obj C)))).v i (i - 1) (by omega) = 0
